stream-readatleast.title: Read a required minimum with Stream.ReadAtLeast
stream-readatleast.short: Handle partial stream reads while filling enough bytes
stream-readatleast.summary: ReadAtLeast accounts for streams returning fewer bytes than requested and keeps reading until the requested minimum is reached or the stream ends.
stream-readatleast.why: Fixed-size headers and similar formats can require a minimum amount without hand-writing a partial-read loop.
stream-readatleast.tips: Choose throwOnEndOfStream deliberately and still use the returned count when early end is allowed.

unsafeaccessor-private-member.title: Access private members directly with UnsafeAccessor
unsafeaccessor-private-member.short: Bind to a known non-public member without runtime reflection
unsafeaccessor-private-member.summary: UnsafeAccessorAttribute binds an extern declaration to a non-public field or method on a target type.
unsafeaccessor-private-member.why: Infrastructure and AOT-sensitive code can access a known private member without runtime reflection overhead.
unsafeaccessor-private-member.tips: This couples code tightly to implementation details. Prefer public APIs and use it only when you control the compatibility risk.

ordered-dictionary-generic.title: Combine key lookup and ordering with OrderedDictionary<TKey,TValue>
ordered-dictionary-generic.short: Use a generic dictionary that also preserves element order
ordered-dictionary-generic.summary: The generic OrderedDictionary supports key-based lookup while retaining a meaningful element order.
ordered-dictionary-generic.why: It fits data that must be queried like a dictionary but displayed or processed in insertion order.
ordered-dictionary-generic.tips: If order has no meaning, Dictionary communicates the requirement more directly.

timeprovider-timestamp.title: Measure elapsed time with TimeProvider timestamps
timeprovider-timestamp.short: Use monotonic elapsed-time APIs through a replaceable time source
timeprovider-timestamp.summary: GetTimestamp and GetElapsedTime calculate elapsed durations using the timestamp source exposed by TimeProvider.
timeprovider-timestamp.why: Code can measure durations without subtracting wall-clock DateTime values while retaining a testable time abstraction.
timeprovider-timestamp.tips: Use GetUtcNow for calendar time and timestamp APIs for elapsed time.

json-options-makereadonly.title: Freeze JSON configuration with JsonSerializerOptions.MakeReadOnly
json-options-makereadonly.short: Explicitly prevent later changes to shared serializer options
json-options-makereadonly.summary: MakeReadOnly transitions JsonSerializerOptions into a read-only state that rejects subsequent configuration changes.
json-options-makereadonly.why: Shared serialization settings gain a clear configuration boundary and cannot be mutated unexpectedly during execution.
json-options-makereadonly.tips: Register converters, naming policies, and other options before freezing the instance.

enum-getvalues-underlying.title: Get enum values in their underlying type
enum-getvalues-underlying.short: Retrieve declared enum values as the underlying integral array
enum-getvalues-underlying.summary: Enum.GetValuesAsUnderlyingType returns the values defined by an enum as an array whose element type is the enum's underlying integral type.
enum-getvalues-underlying.why: Generic tooling that needs numeric representations can avoid per-enum conversion code.
enum-getvalues-underlying.tips: Use Enum.GetValues<TEnum> when enum values and their meaning are what the caller actually needs.

barrier-phases.title: Synchronize worker phases with Barrier
barrier-phases.short: Advance only after every participant reaches the phase boundary
barrier-phases.summary: Barrier waits until all registered participants call SignalAndWait, then advances them to the next phase.
barrier-phases.why: Iterative parallel algorithms can express a point where every worker must finish the current round before continuing.
barrier-phases.tips: Design participant removal and failure paths carefully, and do not force Barrier into ordinary asynchronous workflows.

countdownevent-signal.title: Count worker completions with CountdownEvent
countdownevent-signal.short: Wait until a configured number of Signal calls arrive
countdownevent-signal.summary: CountdownEvent starts with a count, decrements it on Signal, and releases waiters when the count reaches zero.
countdownevent-signal.why: It represents a synchronous join point for several independently completing operations.
countdownevent-signal.tips: Task.WhenAll is usually more natural for Task-based asynchronous work; CountdownEvent is aimed at synchronous coordination.

lazy-thread-safety-mode.title: Choose Lazy<T> concurrency behavior with LazyThreadSafetyMode
lazy-thread-safety-mode.short: Make competing lazy initialization semantics explicit
lazy-thread-safety-mode.summary: LazyThreadSafetyMode controls how Lazy<T> behaves when multiple threads request its value concurrently.
lazy-thread-safety-mode.why: Callers can choose single published initialization or modes that permit competing factory execution according to the use case.
lazy-thread-safety-mode.tips: Factories with side effects need special care with PublicationOnly; prefer the default behavior unless another mode is justified.

unmanagedcallersonly-interop.title: Expose native-callable entry points with UnmanagedCallersOnly
unmanagedcallersonly-interop.short: Mark static managed methods for direct unmanaged invocation
unmanagedcallersonly-interop.summary: UnmanagedCallersOnlyAttribute marks a static method as an entry point that unmanaged code can invoke through a function pointer.
unmanagedcallersonly-interop.why: NativeAOT and low-level interop scenarios can provide callback entry points to native components.
unmanagedcallersonly-interop.tips: This is not for normal managed calls. Match calling conventions and supported parameter types exactly.
